question.text: This man served as president of Princeton from 1902 to 1910 before being elected U.S. president in 1912.
question.clue: Louis Brandeis helped to create his New Freedom platform and he won his second term on the slogan, "He kept us out of war".

swap.text: John T. Scopes was defended by this man, who had earlier successfully defended thrill killers Leopold and Loeb.
swap.clue: This man blamed a cheapness in the valuation of life on the cold killings of World War I in a speech that argued that, in accordance with Nietzsche's philosophy, two men who had devised the "perfect crime" had to commit it.

question.text: The bloodiest battle of the war took place on this Cuban hill, which was near Teddy Roosevelt's Rough Riders and the Buffalo Soldiers on Kettle Hill.
question.clue: Samuel Sumner commanded the cavalry since "Fighting Joe" Wheeler was deathly ill, but Wheeler rose from his sickbed to meet up with Jacob Kent, who had been dispatched by William Rufus Shafter.

swap.leadin: After this event, Max Blanck and Isaac Harris were tried for murder.
swap.text: Name this event, in which the Asch building was set ablaze. During this event, many garment workers were unable to escape because the exterior doors were locked.
swap.clue: Josephine Goldmark and Rose Schneiderman used this event as motivation to continue pressing for better working conditions, and it was investigated by future Labor secretary Frances Perkins.

question.text: This lawyer submitted a famous brief to the Court in the case of Muller v. Oregon arguing for special treatment for women. Justice McReynolds notably refused to speak with him after he was nominated to the Court.
question.clue: This man used a landmark 100-page scientifically-based legal brief compiled by Josephine Goldmark to argue for shorter labor hours for women in Muller v. Oregon.

swap.text: This D. W. Griffith film resparked the popularity of the KKK in the 20th century. This film was controversially shown in the White House by Woodrow Wilson.
swap.clue: The mulatto Lydia Brown causes the disastrous sexual attraction of a prominent senator in one scene, while later Gus forces Flora to jump off a cliff after she rejects his marriage proposal.

question.text: Czolgosz was inspired to support anarchism after hearing this woman speak in Cleveland. Although she did not condone his assassination of William McKinley, she asked, "Who knows but what he, too, was willing to 'fight for his country and die for her liberty?'" in her defense of Czolgosz.
question.clue: She was boycotted by the British left after discussing her horror with Leninism in My Disillusionment in Russia, and her other writings include the periodical Mother Earth.

swap.text: This socialist presidential candidate ran for president five times and ran in 1920 from a prison cell. He helped to found the Industrial Workers of the World with Bill Haywood.
swap.clue: This man later helped found a political party on whose ticket he ran five times.

question.text: This newly appointed Secretary of State under Theodor Roosevelt was at the meeting with college football leaders. This Nobel Prize winner helped secure Japanese agreement for the Open Door Policy in China.
question.clue: He had already worked as McKinley's secretary of war, but his best-known work came in another cabinet post.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about flooding on the Mississippi and Missouri Rivers.
swap.text: The Great Flood of 1927 on the Mississippi spurred this movement of some 6 million African-Americans from the rural south to northern cities such as Chicago.
swap.clue: The most famous series of paintings by Jacob Lawrence depicts this event.

question.leadin: This president declared that "the chief business of the American people is business."
question.text: Name this president who promoted laissez-faire economics despite supporting government intervention as governor of Massachusetts. This "silent" president vetoed the McNary-Haugen Farm Relief Bill while in office.

swap.leadin: McClure's Magazine published many works by journalists known by this term.
swap.text: Teddy Roosevelt used what term to refer to writers who investigated corruption in politics and business at the turn of the 20th century? It suggests one who digs into the metaphorical dirt.
swap.clue: This term was used to describe Henry Demarest Lloyd, the author of Wealth Against Commowealth, which critiqued an organization that was also exposed by Ida Tarbell.

question.text: After being reelected to the House of Representatives, Victor Berger was denied his seat when he was convicted under this act. The phrase "clear and present danger" originated in a case regarding this act.
question.clue: This 1917 legislation that Daniel Ellsberg was accused of violating for stealing and leaking the Pentagon Papers.

swap.leadin: As a result of this, several coal miners armed themselves and attempted to destroy mines in Colorado in the Colorado Coalfield War.
swap.text: Identify this 1914 response of the Colorado National Guard against the strike of the United Mine Workers, which resulted in the death of 11 children and 9 mine workers, named for the mining camp where it took place.
swap.clue: This non-West Virginia incident was worsened by the hired Baldwin-Felts agency.

question.text: Carrie Chapman Catt, the founder of this American organization, encouraged the Icelandic suffragette movement by enlisting Briet Bjarnheðinsdottir ("BREE-yet bjarn-HAY-theens-DOH-teer"). The NAWSA was succeeded by this organization that sponsored the U.S. presidential debates between 1976 and 1984.
question.clue: After winning the right to vote, NAWSA was reconstituted as this advocacy group. Prior to 1988, this group organized U.S. presidential debates.

swap.text: This American chemist enforced the law as head of the USDA's Bureau of Chemistry. He carried out voluntary "poison squad" studies testing the effects of common preservatives like formaldehyde on the human body.
swap.clue: This doctor who advocated for the Pure Food and Drug Act. One of this man's campaigns targeted Coca-Cola for excessive caffeine, which eventually led to his downfall.

question.leadin: In 1995, this union merged with the Amalgamated Clothing and Textile Workers' Union to form the Union of Needletrades, 7 Industrial, and Textile Employees.
question.text: Name this union frst formed in 1900, which led revolts like the "Uprising of 20,000" consisting of Jewish immigrants such as Clara Lemlich, who protested the conditions of females like herself in sweatshops.
question.clue: Founded in 1900, it organized strikes between 1909 and 1911 which eventually led to a settlement that included a "Protocol for Peace."

swap.leadin: Answer stuff about Muckraking classics of the Progressive Era.
swap.text: In this first collection of McClure's magazine articles published by Lincoln Steffens in 1904, he looks at the sources of urban political corruption, writing that the "big business man" is a "self-righteous fraud" who should keep away from politics.

question.leadin: Joseph F. Smith issued the "Second Manifesto" prior to events concerning this senator, during which he testified that he had never sworn an "oath of vengeance."
question.text: Give this Senator from Utah who continued to serve as an apostle after his 1933 defeat by Elbert D. Thomas. Many leading LDS figures were questioned about illegal polygamous marriages during a four-year set of hearings begun by the seating of this Mormon senator.
question.clue: This person is the alphabetically-latter namesake of a bill described as "vicious, extortionate, and obnoxious" by a president who signed it into law anyway, ignoring vigorous opposition from Thomas Lamont, Henry Ford, and over 1,000 economists.

swap.text: This awesome jew, who would later Replace Holmes on the Supreme Court, wrote the opinion in Pfalsgraf. He also wrote a notable concurrence to Schechter Poultry and the book Paradoxes of Legal Science.
swap.clue: After eighteen years of revolutionizing many areas of the common law from the New York Court of Appeals, this man was appointed to the Supreme Court by Herbert Hoover.
